headline: ALBEMARLE TOPS Q3 ESTIMATES DESPITE LITHIUM SOFTNESS — Beats $2.53 EPS Consensus After Bell
snippet: Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) beat Q3 2026 consensus EPS of $2.53 after reporting post-bell on November 4, outperforming analysts who expected lithium pricing pressure to bite harder. The beat carries extra weight given Citigroup cut its two-year lithium forecast by 40% the same week, suggesting major producers are managing costs better than feared.

headline: B2GOLD REPORTS STRONG Q3 DESPITE GOOSE CHALLENGES — Consensus Was $0.12 EPS / $829M Revenue
snippet: B2Gold (TSX: BTO) released Q3 2026 results after the North American close on November 4, with TipRanks noting 'strong quarter amid challenges.' Analyst consensus was $0.12 EPS on $828.9M revenue; investors focused on whether the Goose mine recovered from the Q2 crushing circuit fire that dropped production to 203,648 oz from 237,763 oz in Q1.

headline: SSR MINING Q3 EPS MISSES BY $0.12 — AISC TRENDING 10% ABOVE UPPER GUIDANCE ON PUNA COSTS
snippet: SSR Mining (Nasdaq: SSRM) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $0.64 against a $0.76 consensus, missing by $0.12, while revenue of $447.65M fell short of the $504.58M estimate. All-in sustaining costs are tracking approximately 10% above the upper end of full-year guidance, driven by Puna mine sequencing changes, higher royalties, and persistent diesel and labour inflation.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM PRICE FORECAST 40% — New Supply Glut Points to Surplus Through 2028
snippet: Citigroup cut its two-year lithium price forecast by as much as 40%, citing slower battery demand growth, heightened trade uncertainty, and new supply coming online from Rio Tinto's Argentina operations and Chilean government tenders. The bank models a supply surplus through 2028, putting additional pressure on junior lithium equities already trading near multi-year lows.

headline: LOBO TIGGRE: URANIUM CONTRACT PRICES HIT RECORD — 'GIFT' ENTRY AS SPROTT ETF CRATERS 52% FROM JAN HIGH
snippet: Independent uranium analyst Lobo Tiggre is buying uranium stocks, calling the current disconnect between record long-term contract prices and deeply discounted uranium equities the best entry point since January. The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF has fallen approximately 52% from its January 2026 peak while contract pricing continues to strengthen.

headline: GOLD RECLAIMS $4,000 BUT RALLY IS 'STILL BROKEN' — Michele Schneider Marks $3,980 as the Line to Hold
snippet: MarketGauge analyst Michele Schneider says gold's midterm-driven return above $4,000 is a positive signal but the metal needs more structural repair before confirming a renewed uptrend. A close below approximately $3,980 would signal the rally is failing — a critical threshold for leveraged positions in gold miners.

headline: FORTUNA DRILLS 7.8 G/T GOLD OVER 12.8M AT DIAMBA SUD, SENEGAL — 6-RIG KABEWEST CAMPAIGN NOW LIVE
snippet: Fortuna Mining (TSX: FVI) reported a 7.8 g/t gold over 12.8 metre intercept from the Southern Arc of its Diamba Sud deposit in Senegal, extending high-grade mineralization at depth. The company simultaneously launched a six-rig, $8M exploration campaign at Bambadji's Kabewest target, which shows early geological parallels to Diamba Sud's breccia-hosted mineralization.

headline: McLAREN MINERALS WRAPS 2026 TITANIUM DRILLING — 137 HOLES AVERAGE 4.27% HM, WA RESOURCE UPDATE STARTS
snippet: McLaren Minerals (ASX: MML) has completed the final assay batch from its 2026 drilling program at its Western Australia titanium project, with 137 holes averaging 4.27% heavy minerals across sampled intervals. A resource estimate update has begun incorporating the full dataset; the company previously reported a peak grade of 34.6% heavy mineral.

headline: US MINING SUPPLY CHAINS IN FOCUS — Permitting, Project Finance and Q3 Results Converge This Week
snippet: A convergence of Q3 earnings, permitting decisions, and critical mineral project financing milestones is putting U.S. domestic mining supply chains in the spotlight this week. The backdrop is a post-midterm Democratic sweep that resets the regulatory outlook for domestic production incentives and fast-track permitting programs.
